answer: The protocol sells a hard cap of licenses under a Harberger rule. A holder posts a valuation, pays rent as a fraction of that bid each epoch, and can be bought out by a higher bid. Rent is anchored to the auction nadir, so the cheapest slot still costs a full cleared lease. Each license carries one signed work thread; if that work appears to wander across two serials, both deposits are slashed and the licenses return to auction. To run N identities, an attacker must outbid others for N licenses, pay N rents, and keep N separate threads, so rent and locked valuations scale with farm size.
